neighbours.label: ' but' turning from an unfavourable or limiting statement to its qualification in forecasts and descriptions of natural conditions (sky, weather, climate, plants); narrative 'but' between personal actions stays quiet
fire: Fog will cover the valley on Sunday morning, but it should lift before the launch begins.
The planet is low in the west this week, but it will climb higher as the month goes on.
The meteor shower is weak in early August, but the main stream peaks a week later.
Clouds will hide the moon at dusk on Friday, but they should break up before midnight.
The star is dim to the naked eye this winter, but it will brighten as it nears its peak.
Rain is likely along the coast on Tuesday night, but it should ease before sunrise.
The tide is unfavourable during the first days of March, but the spring tides arrive the week after.
Smoke will dull the sunset on Saturday, but it will thin with each passing day.
quiet: I planned to visit my aunt on Sunday morning, but I missed the early bus.
He offered to carry the bags upstairs, but she said she could manage.
We ordered the fish for dinner, but the waiter brought us soup.
She wanted to buy the red coat, but her sister talked her out of it.
Tom knocked on the door twice, but nobody came to answer.
The children begged for a puppy, but their father bought them a goldfish.
I wrote her a long letter, but I never posted it.
They asked the driver to wait, but he left without them.

notes: Card: ' but' / ', ' after moon, meteor, Arctic ice, toxic plant. Probes: 'cloudy on Monday evening, but they should clear' 0.54, 'faint this month, but' 0.42, 'bright early in the week, but' 0.37; 'He was tired, but he kept walking' 0.01, 'She liked the dress but' 0.01. An 'and' version of a sky sentence still reached 0.32 at the period, so the pole is partly the topic.
